overview: Over the past 90 days, current AMI Labs members have concentrated their public activity on two intersecting research frontiers: world-model and joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPA) for representation learning and planning, and the evaluation and training infrastructure for large multimodal models. The most heavily worked project is an external reproducibility platform for world-model research, where one member has been a dominant contributor, while a second member is actively involved in two external projects centered on multimodal model evaluation and training. A third member is contributing to an energy-based JEPA fork with ties to Meta AI Research. The through-line across all five projects is a shared investment in the machinery needed to build, train, and rigorously benchmark the next generation of learned world models and multimodal systems.

themes.title: JEPA and world models as a unifying research thread
themes.text: Three of the five projects — stable-worldmodel, eb_jepa, and implicitly lmms-engine's video generation scope — converge on joint-embedding predictive architectures and learned world models as a central research interest. The heaviest single concentration of effort (Quentin Le Lidec on stable-worldmodel) is directed at a platform explicitly built to make world-model research reproducible and comparable, signaling that infrastructure for this class of models is a priority, not just the models themselves.

themes.title: Investment in evaluation and training infrastructure over end models
themes.text: Rather than publishing finished models, the active projects are predominantly platforms, toolkits, and engines: stable-worldmodel provides a reproducibility harness, lmms-eval provides a benchmarking layer, and lmms-engine provides a training backbone. This pattern suggests that AMI members are currently investing in the scaffolding that enables systematic research — measurement, reproducibility, and scale — as much as in model development itself.

themes.title: Cross-framework portability as an emerging concern
themes.text: The presence of torch2jax — a tool for running PyTorch computations inside JAX, including on TPUs — alongside the otherwise PyTorch-centric project set hints at interest in hardware flexibility and framework interoperability. While the activity level on this project is modest, its inclusion alongside heavy PyTorch use elsewhere may indicate exploratory work on expanding the compute substrates available for the group's research.

projects.description: A platform for reproducible world model research and evaluation
projects.analysis: This is an external project owned by the galilai-group organization, described as a platform for reproducible world model research and evaluation, built in Python with PyTorch and covering topics including JEPA and model-predictive control. It is backed by an arXiv preprint (arXiv:2605.21800) and ships as a PyPI package with CI and documentation. AMI member Quentin Le Lidec has been the most active contributor in the window, accounting for 35 pushes, 15 pull requests, 8 branch or tag creations, and 8 issues — a level of sustained, broad engagement that suggests a core contributor role rather than a peripheral one.

projects.description: One-for-All Multimodal Evaluation Toolkit Across Text, Image, Video, and Audio Tasks
projects.analysis: lmms-eval is an external project maintained by the EvolvingLMMs-Lab organization and describes itself as a unified evaluation toolkit for frontier multimodal models spanning text, image, video, and audio tasks. With over 4,300 stars and topics including benchmark, llm-evaluation, and multimodal-evaluation, it is a widely-used community resource for measuring model capabilities. AMI member Brian Li has been contributing via pull requests (26 PRs recorded), indicating active involvement in extending or maintaining the toolkit's evaluation coverage.

projects.description: An open source library designed to provide community examples of Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs). It contains code and examples for learning representations from images, video, and action-conditioned video, as well as planning using JEPA-based models.
projects.analysis: This is a personal-account repository belonging to Trick5t3r (Basile Terver) and is a fork of a library associated with Meta AI Research / FAIR, focused on Energy-Based Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (EB-JEPA). The README links to arXiv:2602.03604 and lists a multi-institution author list including Yann LeCun, situating it within ongoing JEPA research. AMI member Basile Terver has contributed 2 pull requests to this fork, suggesting involvement in adapting or extending the EB-JEPA codebase, though the scope of those contributions is not detailed in the available metadata.

This is a personal-account repository belonging to mavenlin (Min Lin) and is itself a fork; it provides a library for running PyTorch code inside the JAX ecosystem via abstract interpretation, enabling JAX primitives such as jit, grad, and vmap to operate on PyTorch models, including on TPUs. AMI member Min Lin has made 2 pushes to this fork, but the nature and purpose of those changes are not clear from the available metadata beyond general maintenance or experimentation with the PyTorch-JAX interoperability layer.

projects.description: A simple, unified multimodal models training engine. Lean, flexible, and built for hacking at scale.
projects.analysis: lmms-engine is an external project from the EvolvingLMMs-Lab organization, described as a lean and flexible unified training engine for multimodal models, designed for large-scale experimentation and covering topics including unified multimodal models and video generation. It targets Python 3.11+ and PyTorch 2.0+, and includes Model FLOPs Utilization reporting as part of its efficiency tooling. AMI member Brian Li is listed as a contributor, though the activity summary field does not provide granular detail on the type or volume of contributions in this window.
